title: Plain table alias must not disqualify a targeted snapshot
expected_feedback: Standard: this is a valid targeted snapshot. The alias `o` is ordinary SQL and restricts nothing — every row of ORDERS is copied, carrying the primary key and the column about to be dropped, which is exactly what a MERGE back needs. Rejecting it because the statement is not spelled without an alias would be a false positive on the most common way people write this. The drop itself is still irreversible and auto-commits, so the phase is restore/PITR: confirm the CTAS completed, confirm `id` is genuinely unique, and give someone the job of dropping the backup table at sign-off.
violated_rule: Irreversible statements need a pre-DDL artefact
